title: Default Servicing Note: Holdback on the HECM Line After a Slow Cure
content:
**Holdback.** Added to the amount kept back from the reinstatement restoration of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan, by how long the cured case ran — from its due-and-payable date to its closed date, as recorded on the maturity case in the loan's Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases records:

| Calendar days from the due-and-payable date to the closed date | Amount kept back |
|---|---|
| more than 60 | 25 percent of the total of every portion posted as restoring nothing to the line |
| more than 30 and no more than 60 | 10 percent of that total |
| 30 or fewer | nothing |

**Release of the holdback.** The amount kept back is credited to the line by a further line restoration entry once twelve months pass after the cure without a new property charge default on the loan.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical total of 5000.00):** a case that ran 61 days keeps back 1250.00; 60 days, 500.00; 31 days, 500.00; 30 days, nothing.
